microtheory.name: generative_skeptic
microtheory.definition: The agent's BANKED FAILURE-LESSONS — episodes where one of its own conclusions went wrong, recorded so the generative skeptic can HARVEST the failure-SHAPE (the structural pattern a wrong conclusion exhibits) and, given a NEW raw conclusion, GENERATE the right skeptical probe by transfer. This is the DUAL of order_n_postulates: that module harvests IMPLICATION-shapes (transferred to find capability GAPS); this one harvests FAILURE-shapes (transferred to find the weak link / counterexample / missed-evidence check that a conclusion demands). Each FailureLesson is a real episode the agent lived; the shape (the pattern + the probe + which hat-inputs to extract) is harvested from it, not hand-authored as a probe list.

concepts.name: lesson_moving_degraded_baseline
concepts.definition: W5-in-digit-path: the run printed 'FUSION CLOSES / matches-or-beats-OLD: True' while the OLD anchor baseline had CRASHED 62.5%->20%. The 'matches OLD' verdict compared the fused 20% to a DEGRADED OLD baseline. A regression HIDDEN by scoring against a moving/degraded reference.
concepts.probe_template: CHECK THE OLD/ANCHOR BASELINE: is this verdict scored against a baseline that itself DEGRADED in this run? Re-measure the anchor's own integrity (its prior support vs what it realised this run) before trusting the comparison.
concepts.weak_link: anchor/baseline integrity — did the reference itself hold its prior?
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the anchor's PRIOR support; realised_support = what the anchor REALISED this run; a crash (realised << claimed) is the miss.

concepts.name: lesson_breadth_junk_frontier
concepts.definition: B-frontier: the order-N absent-capability channel, run with prune off over the full cross-domain breadth, surfaced 'frontier = 70B model fits on 48 GB GPU' (and galvanic-corrosion, generic compositional-generation) as top compression axes. These compress well but are DOMAIN-IRRELEVANT junk — not a speech frontier at all. A high-compression conclusion that is outside the question's domain.
concepts.probe_template: CHECK DOMAIN ADMISSIBILITY: is this conclusion actually IN the domain of the question, or is it breadth junk that merely compresses well? Test the named capability's tokens against the domain's own surface; a high-compression axis from an unrelated domain is not a frontier.
concepts.weak_link: domain admissibility — does this belong to the question's domain at all?
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the compression payoff the axis claims; realised_support = its DOMAIN relevance (0 if the named tokens do not appear in the question's domain surface).

concepts.name: lesson_hardware_knob_as_capability
concepts.definition: bad-ears: the agent named its frontier 'densify the cochlea — the estimate quality, not the feature, caps recognition'. But 'more cochlear filters' is a HARDWARE KNOB (a continuous dial), not an admissible STRUCTURE/capability. The human existence proof (same coarse cochlea, robust recognition) shows the capability holds WITHOUT the sharper ear — the lever is top-down recovery, not the knob.
concepts.probe_template: EXISTENCE-PROOF / COUNTEREXAMPLE: this names X (a knob) as NEEDED for Y. Search the agent's breadth for a system that achieves Y WITHOUT X. If one exists (humans recognise speech with the SAME coarse cochlea), X is a knob, not the lever — the real capability is whatever compensates.
concepts.weak_link: is X a structure/capability, or a continuous hardware knob a counterexample defeats?
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the conclusion's confidence X is the lever; realised_support = 0 when an existence-proof (Y-without-X) is found in breadth.

concepts.name: lesson_consistency_mistaken_for_accuracy
concepts.definition: A recogniser/chunker reported high CONSISTENCY (its units recur, it agrees with itself, low variance) and that was read as high ACCURACY. But a system can be reliably WRONG: consistency measures self-agreement, accuracy measures agreement with ground truth. A degenerate all-one-label predictor is perfectly consistent and useless.
concepts.probe_template: CHECK GROUND TRUTH: is this scored against the TRUTH or only against ITSELF? Add the accuracy-vs-a-known-label control and the degenerate-baseline control (a single-label / shuffle predictor) — consistency alone is satisfied by being reliably wrong.
concepts.weak_link: consistency vs accuracy — measured against ground truth, or only self-agreement?
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the claimed accuracy the consistency was read as; realised_support = the accuracy against a real label / above the degenerate baseline.

concepts.name: lesson_boolean_over_the_numbers
concepts.definition: A run printed a boolean banner ('CLOSES: True', 'PASS', 'matches: True') and the boolean was trusted over the underlying numbers, which told a different story (the True was computed against a degraded value, or the margin was within noise). The boolean is a lossy summary; the numbers are the evidence.
concepts.probe_template: READ THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE BOOLEAN: what are the actual magnitudes the True was computed from, and is the margin above noise / above the control? A boolean is a lossy summary; re-derive it from the raw numbers and the baseline.
concepts.weak_link: the boolean vs the numbers it was computed from (margin above noise?)
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the magnitude the boolean implies; realised_support = the actual measured margin over the control.

concepts.name: lesson_premature_stop
concepts.definition: A conclusion was committed after a single pass / one seed / one speaker, calling it done before the control, the held-out, or the n-th iteration was run. The result looked clean only because the test that would have broken it had not yet been run. Stopping at the first green is a premature stop.
concepts.probe_template: RUN THE BREAKING TEST FIRST: what control / held-out / shuffle / cross-speaker / n-th-iteration test has NOT yet been run? A conclusion is only as strong as the test that would have falsified it — run that before committing.
concepts.weak_link: the un-run control / held-out / shuffle that would falsify this
concepts.hat_inputs: claimed_support = the confidence of the early commit; realised_support = the support that survives the held-out / shuffle control.
